subject: Segmentation visualization and compact isolation package for Dedicated/Private
messages:
From: Dana Spencer <dana.spencer@acme.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: compact topology + isolation matrix for Dedicated/Private

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this on. Acme has an internal readiness review on May 10 and our auditors want a short (executive + technical) package describing how Redwood isolates Dedicated and Private deployments from other tenants and from the public control plane. Specifically we need:

- One-page visual topology (simple diagram that can go in an executive slide) showing customer-dedicated GPU pools, control plane separation, and egress choke points.
- A compact CSV-style isolation matrix mapping Redwood services (serving runtime, control plane, metrics, backups) to network zones and trust boundaries.
- A short CAIQ/SIG crosswalk that points to where controls are implemented (or planned).

Can you deliver a compact package (PDF diagram + isolation CSV + one-page CAIQ crosswalk) by EOD May 4? We want something concise — auditors don’t want the whole architecture packet, just a tight summary and a tech contact for a follow-up call.

If you need a sample format I can share ours, but an internal Redwood template would be ideal.

Appreciate the help — this is timeboxed.

—Dana
Dana Spencer
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Corp

Attachments: none

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dana Spencer <dana.spencer@acme.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: compact topology + isolation matrix for Dedicated/Private

Dana — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the deliverables you listed. Plan:

- Deliver a one-page topology PDF (executive-friendly) + layered technical zoom PDF.
- Provide a CSV isolation matrix (service -> zone -> control) and a one-page CAIQ crosswalk (.docx).
- Offer a 30-minute walkthrough the week of May 5 if auditors want a quick Q&A.

Looping in Olga (security architect) and Neha (network/infra) to produce the artifacts and validate wording for SIG/CAIQ tieouts. Ben is on the thread for any procurement/contract notes we should surface.

Olga/Neha: target for a first draft is EOD May 3 so we can iterate and send final by EOD May 4. If dates need adjusting, say so now.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 08:45:00 -07:00

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 10:03 AM jonas.weber@redwood.com wrote:
> Dana — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the deliverables you listed.

Dana / team — sharing a tech-first draft for internal review. Attachments are preliminary and marked v1: guarded-topology-v1.pdf (compact topology with annotated trust boundaries) and isolation-matrix-v1.csv (comma-delimited mapping of services to network zones and controls). Also drafting the CAIQ crosswalk as a short doc (will attach v1 on Monday).

Key notes to call out in the executive summary (short bullets we recommend):
- Dedicated/Private customers get isolated GPU pools (customer-tagged pools) with network-level tenant fencing.
- Control plane is logically segregated: customer management plane endpoints are behind a private control-plane tier for Private deployments and routed via a separate tenancy for Dedicated.
- Egress filter enforcement at perimeter subnets + centralized proxy for optional content inspection.
- KV/Crypto operations use customer-specific KMS keyspaces (integration with customer KMS for Private; HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated where requested).
- Auditable flow: per-request tracing metadata + retention window configurable per account; logs pushed to customer-managed sinks on Private requests where requested.

Open questions:
- Acme: do you want the topology to show shared-but-isolated monitoring / or exclude monitoring from the executive view? (We usually omit monitoring from exec slide and include it in the tech appendix.)
- Neha: can you confirm egress CIDR filtering options for Dedicated pools? I will annotate the matrix with the final values once confirmed.

Attachments (stubs):
- guarded-topology-v1.pdf (diagram, 1 page)
- isolation-matrix-v1.csv (columns: service,network_zone,trust_boundary,controls,notes)

Olga Petrov
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dana Spencer <dana.spencer@acme.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: compact topology + isolation package (attached)

Dana — attaching the compact package per your request. Deliverables attached: guarded-topology-v1.pdf, isolation-matrix-v1.csv, and a short CAIQ crosswalk (caiq-crosswalk-short.docx).

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Redwood’s Dedicated and Private offerings enforce multi-layered isolation: customer-dedicated GPU pools and tenant fencing at the serving layer; a logically separated control plane for customer management; perimeter and subnet-level egress filtering; and cryptographic separation for keys and backups. Where customers require, we provide customer-managed sinks and KMS integration to meet compliance objectives.

Key bullet callouts (for auditor review):
- Serving isolation: per-tenant GPU assignment + per-tenant runtime namespaces and KV cache partitioning.
- Control plane: separate logical tenancy and routing for control traffic; limited management endpoints per customer.
- Network: dedicated VPCs or dedicated VPC stacks for Private deployments, explicit egress ACLs, NAT/proxy chokepoints, and route tables documented in the CSV.
- Data protection: KMS partitioning for customer keys, HSM-backed root keys for high-assurance Dedicated customers, and customer-configurable retention windows.

Attached files (stubs): guarded-topology-v1.pdf (PDF diagram), isolation-matrix-v1.csv (CSV), caiq-crosswalk-short.docx (DOCX). If the auditors want a 30-minute walkthrough, we can schedule May 6–7 in the morning (PDT).

Thanks — we’re standing by for any small edits.

--

Principal Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
